messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west1-gpu-pool queue depth spike detected (p50 latency > 1200ms, queue length 14k). Autoscaler attempted +20 nodes but hit project quota. Some requests returning 503/504 from edge routing. Escalation level: P1. Paging @oncall-jamie :rotating_light:
jamie: saw the alert, joining. Can someone dump autoscaler logs and pool quota?
sasha: looks like quotaExceeded errors from cloud-provider during scale up window. snippet: `Error: quotaExceeded: requested 32 GPUs, available 16`
miguel: confirming — quota for us-west1 GPUs at project level is 24 total across Dedicated pools, autoscaler tried to go to 48 for burst.
jamie: ack. Impact? Are clients seeing throttles or silent latencies?
tilly: alerting shows 7% 5xx rate overall across hosted API for the last 6m, spikes concentrated in us-west1 region routes (route shard usw-prod-1). Some requests spilled to eu-west1 and eu logs show increased tail latency.
jamie: ok, action plan: 1) toggle routing policy to favor us-east1 warm-standby for best-effort spillover, 2) if routing change unsafe, carve a safe subset of customers to route to lower-capacity models as fallback, 3) open GCP quota increase (but that'll be slow). Who can run the routing override? @sasha?
sasha: I can run a manual steer. Preparing command to update routing policy: ```json
{
  "policy": "region_preference",
  "order": ["us-east1","eu-west1","us-west1"],
  "weight_overrides": {"us-east1":10}
}
```
jamie: wait — don't flip fully. Let's do incremental: weight_overrides us-east1 +3, reduce us-west1 by -3. We want graceful drain.
sasha: applying incremental override now. Executing: `redwoodctl routing apply --policy regional --set us-east1=+3 us-west1=-3`
sasha: done. Observability: queue in us-west1 down from 14k -> 9k in 90s. p50 latency improved ~400ms.
miguel: still seeing autoscaler errors in logs: `scale attempt aborted: insufficient project quota`. Manual provisioning would need quota increase or temporary reassign of capacity from lower-priority pools. I can try evicting batch-worker pool to free GPUs for critical. Thoughts?
jamie: what is the customer impact if we evict batch-worker? Batch is internal ML training jobs, low priority for next 2 hours. Approve if it frees enough to bring us-west under threshold.
tilly: batch workers currently use 12 GPUs in us-west1. Evicting would free 12. If we reroute +3 weight to us-east1 and free 12 GPUs, we should be okay for the next 45-90m.
sasha: manual reroute stable. I'll keep an eye on error surface.
miguel: starting eviction of batch-worker pool: `orchestrator drain --pool batch-worker --region us-west1 --evict=true`
miguel: eviction completed, 12 GPUs freed. Autoscaler retried and succeeded partially; pool scaled +10 nodes, queue now 3.1k. 5xx rate down to 2.1%.
jamie: good. We should also flip a temporary circuit-breaker to reduce request inflight per connection in us-west1 to avoid queue rebuild. Set per-route concurrency cap to 2 for high-cost routes: `redwoodctl routes update --concurrency-cap 2 --selector cost>0.5 --region us-west1`
sasha: applied. Observability shows slow but steady recovery.
oncall-rotation-bot: Heads-up: jamie is mid-shift and will hand off to tilly in ~25m. Confirming on-call handoff procedure.
jamie: proceeding with handoff protocol. Tilly, summary: cause = project GPU quota in us-west1 prevented autoscaler from scaling, autoscaler retried and aborted; mitigation = immediate routing weight shift to us-east1 (+3), eviction of batch-worker freed 12 GPUs, manual scale succeeded, applied concurrency caps; customer impact = ~7% 5xx at peak, primarily short-lived, now ~2.1%. Next steps = request quota increase, create placement policy to reserve emergency burst pool, postmortem.
tilly: understood. Any customer-facing incidents required? Should we page success/incident update to SRE-runbook?
jamie: create SEV note and start incident ticket. I'll draft a short customer note: "We experienced a regional capacity shortage in us-west1 causing elevated error rates for a subset of requests. We've restored capacity by rerouting and reallocating internal capacity; we are requesting quota increases to prevent recurrence."
sasha: just observed a small regression: eu-west1 tail latency rose as it absorbed extra traffic, but within SLO for now. Monitoring.
miguel: filed support ticket with cloud provider for quota increase (case: 231-WS1-QUOTA). ETA unknown. Also opened internal infra ticket to build reserved emergency pool.
jamie: handoff: tilly you're on call. Current responder list: tilly (primary), sasha (routing), miguel (infra). Keep monitoring for 2hr burn-down window. If queue > 5k again or 5xx > 4% escalate to oncall-backfill.
tilly: taking over. Thanks Jamie. Will keep slack thread updated.
(35m later) tilly: follow-up: metrics stable, queue us-west1 450 -> 220 -> 80, 5xx at 1.3%. Routing weight rollback plan: slowly move weight back to default over next 30m.
tilly: rolling back override: `redwoodctl routing apply --policy regional --set us-east1=-2 us-west1=+2`
tilly: rollback complete. Observability: no spike.
tilly: created incident ticket INC-2026-309 with summary and attached early triage notes. Assigned to eng-infra for reserved pool design.
jamie: great work everyone. We'll include root cause: project-level GPU quota constraint + autoscaler no graceful fallback on quota errors. Action items: (1) quota increase (miguel), (2) emergency reserved pool design (eng-infra), (3) autoscaler improvement to surface quota errors earlier and trigger routing fallback (eng-runtime), (4) customer communication draft (ops).
sasha: adding a small fix — autoscaler should annotate nodes with scaling failure reason in metrics so routing policy rule can act automatically. Filed GH issue #3820.
tilly: I'll post a short incident update to #status and tag customers with affected SLAs.
miguel: uploading logs and link to runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/incident-gpu-quota. Also attaching `kubectl get pods` snippet and autoscaler logs to INC-2026-309.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-309 created and linked to thread. Severity: P1 -> P2 (mitigated). Notes: manual reroute + eviction performed.
jamie: closing handoff. Will follow up for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
